question: Why did bare Al outperform the carbon/Al current collector at 4 mA/cm^2, and how much lower was its hysteresis?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE regexp_matches(text, '4 ?mA|hysteresis|overpotential|bare|outperform|Coulombic', 'i') ORDER BY page, line_no

SELECT id, figure_id, statement, value, unit, condition FROM figure_facts WHERE statement ILIKE '%hysteresis%' OR statement ILIKE '%4 mA%' OR statement ILIKE '%bare%' OR statement ILIKE '%overpotential%'
SELECT id, page, line_no, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (3,5) ORDER BY page, line_no

SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (1,2) AND (text ILIKE '%bare%' OR text ILIKE '%hysteresis%' OR text ILIKE '%shorting%' OR text ILIKE '%fail%' OR text ILIKE '%mV%' OR text ILIKE '%Cu %' OR text ILIKE '%Figure 1c%' OR text ILIKE '%cycling%') ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page=2 AND line_no BETWEEN 50 AND 90 ORDER BY line_no

The document does not support that premise. It does not report bare Al outperforming the carbon/Al collector at the high current. At that current, the paper says the opposite: bare Al electrodes were prone to failure at these currents[1]. The carbon/Al collector, by contrast, kept a low hysteresis there: with a 45 mV hysteresis[2] at 4 mA/cm^2[3].

Why bare Al did worse: the paper attributes the bare Al shorting to uneven plating caused by a higher nucleation overpotential: we attribute to the uneven plating that occurs due to the higher[4] nucleation overpotential[5]. The carbon layer lowers that barrier: is reduced from 19 to 12 mV by the carbon layer[6].

How much lower the hysteresis was: the document gives no hysteresis value for bare Al at the high current, so no difference can be calculated. The only hysteresis comparison it makes at that current is with earlier Cu electrodes, which nearly double the hysteresis at[7] 4 mA/cm^2[8] (Figure S4), so that comparison is not with bare Al.
